subject: Inference capacity playbook review - scheduling
message_1_body:
Hi Maggie and team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this month — great questions on burst isolation and predictable latency. Wed like to run a focused technical deep-dive to walk through a proposed capacity playbook for your Dedicated deployment: pool sizing guidance, autoscale patterns (thresholds, warm pools, burst), and isolation strategies for multi-tenant workloads.

Proposed agenda (45-60 min):
- 5m introductions and objectives
- 15m current workload profile review (seq len, qps, latency SLOs)
- 15m recommended pool sizing & quantization tradeoffs
- 10m autoscale + warm-pool orchestration
- 10m isolation, fallback, and cost guardrails
- 5m action items

I attached a draft capacity runbook and a short agenda. Can you confirm who from Atlas should join (ops, security, procurement)? For timing, we have these windows next week (PDT):
- Tue 2027-05-26 09:00-10:00
- Tue 2027-05-26 15:00-16:00
- Wed 2027-05-27 10:30-11:30

If none work, propose two alternatives and well adjust.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

Attachment: capacity_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 18 pages)
message_2_subject: Re: Inference capacity playbook review - scheduling
message_2_body:
Irene,

Thanks for putting this together. Confirming we should include:
- concrete autoscale thresholds (e.g., warm pool warmup times, target p95 CPU/GPU utilization)
- KV cache sizing and eviction policies for chat workloads
- fallback policies to lower-cost model variants when capacity is constrained

I can cover autoscale orchestration and the warm pool runbook.

Prefer Tue 2027-05-26 15:00-16:00 PT — that keeps overlap with our EU team for recording. If Atlas prefers Wed morning, Im available Wed 10:30 as well.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
